note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment decision following recent PSA rise to 10.0 ng/mL and confirmation of prior prostate cancer diagnosis.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. The patient is a 56-year-old retired bus driver, currently living independently in a retirement community with his wife. He has a medical history of hypertension and hypercholesterolaemia, managed with valsartan, metoprolol, and atorvastatin. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 1/35. He engages in light weight-training at home twice weekly and consumes approximately 7 units of alcohol per week. Recent appointments include a pain clinic visit for chronic shoulder pain and routine podiatry care. He has previously declined participation in research trials.

Per rectum, a palpable nodule is noted in the left lateral aspect of the prostate, consistent with a clinical T2a stage. The prostate is otherwise symmetrically enlarged. General examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs.

admin: Patient declined research participation previously; respect for AS-related trials.
